fields.hero_description: Get an automotive landing page that books test drives and service visits, with every lead saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Sits Behind Each Automotive Page
fields.features_subheading: A shopper sees one car or one offer. Behind it, six parts decide who follows up and where the lead is kept.
fields.feature_1:
One prompt for the page and its lead table

Describe the car or the offer and what a shopper should do next. Emergent builds the page and the table its leads land in, then changes either one when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Each lead sent to one named person

Name who follows up on each kind of request, such as a sales consultant for test drives. That person gets a Slack message or an email with every answer the shopper gave.
fields.feature_3:
Leads copied into your CRM

HubSpot or any other CRM with an API receives each lead along with the page it came from. The sales team keeps working in the same CRM it already opens every morning.
fields.feature_4:
Price cuts and sold cars by message

Tell Emergent to drop the price by $1,500 or mark the car sold. The page changes at the same web address, and every lead collected before the change stays in the table.
fields.feature_5:
A page for each vehicle or service offer

Ask for one page per car on the lot or per seasonal service special. Every page writes to the same lead table, and each row there records the page each request came from.
fields.feature_6:
Your dealership's domain and the code

Your dealership's custom domain is included and uses credits. On paid plans, the pages export to your own GitHub repository together with their lead table and routing rules.

fields.usecase_heading: Automotive Landing Pages by Lead Type
fields.tab_content_1:
Three Saturday test drive slots on one SUV's page

Brightwater Auto's page for a used 2021 hybrid SUV puts the $24,900 price and the 41,200 miles above 3 Saturday slots. Nadia Pruitt picked 10:30 AM. Sales consultant Wes Talbot got her booking as a Slack direct message, and the SUV was washed and parked out front when she arrived.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each trade-in under 60,000 miles is seen that day

Owners asking Kestrel Valley Motors for a trade-in number enter the VIN and the mileage, then describe the condition. Every trade-in under 60,000 miles goes on used car manager Ines Varga's list that day, marked Same day. Cars at 60,000 miles or more get an email asking for 4 photos and show Photos requested.
fields.tab_content_3:
A $49 brake inspection booked into a bay time

Drivers who click Corbin Street Garage's ad for a $49 brake inspection pick a bay time on the page instead of calling the shop. The service writer starts each morning with one table of bookings, 14 of them this week, each listing the car and the time it is due in.
fields.tab_content_4:
When a ride-and-drive slot fills, the page closes it

On Saturday, Halden Ridge EV runs a ride-and-drive event in 4 time slots of 12 seats each. Visitors choose a slot and leave a name and a phone number. A slot that reaches 12 seats shows Full and stops taking signups. By Thursday, 41 of 48 seats were taken, and the count on the page moved with every RSVP.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an Automotive Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan an automotive landing page around one car or offer, keep its price claims within the rules, and route every lead.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one car or one offer
fields.howto_step_1_des: A page for a single SUV and a page for a brake special ask different things of the visitor. Give each one its own page, and decide the one action it asks for: a test drive time, a trade-in request, or a bay booking.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the ad's vehicle or offer in the headline, in the same words and at the same price. A driver who clicked a $49 brake inspection and lands on a full service menu has to hunt for the deal before booking anything.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The FTC Used Car Rule says a dealer must display a Buyers Guide on a used vehicle before offering it for sale to a consumer. The guide may come off during a test drive and goes back on when the drive is over. Note that in the booking message.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Under Regulation Z, a credit ad that states the amount of any payment must also state the down payment, the repayment terms, and the annual percentage rate. Give a monthly figure on the page the same treatment, or show the cash price alone.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask only what the follow-up needs
fields.howto_step_5_des: A test drive needs a name and a time, plus a phone number to confirm it. A trade-in needs the VIN and the mileage, since those two decide who looks at it first. Leave credit questions for the showroom, where a person can explain each one.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide before launch who gets test drive bookings, who prices trade-ins, and who covers Saturdays. Agree on how soon a lead hears back. A booking that nobody confirms leaves the shopper free to book a drive at another lot.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Tag every ad link with its source. Each Monday, put bookings next to the shoppers who came in, source by source. A page with plenty of bookings and few visits needs a reminder the day before more than it needs more traffic.

faq_plan.q: What is an automotive landing page?
faq_plan.a: An automotive landing page is a single web page built around one vehicle or one offer, such as a used SUV or a service special. It asks the visitor for one action, like booking a test drive, and leaves out the full inventory and the site menu. Nothing on it pulls the shopper away from that action.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an automotive landing page?
faq_plan.a: Tell Emergent's AI landing page builder what you are selling, what a shopper should do, and who should hear about it. Emergent builds the page with a lead database you own, and you change any part by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should automotive landing pages show on the first screen?
faq_plan.a: The vehicle or the offer with its price, and the one button you want pressed. Automotive landing pages for a single car add the mileage and a real photo of that car on the lot, not a stock image. Put the booking slots or the form on the first phone screen as well.

faq_plan.q: Should an auto landing page keep the dealership's site menu?
faq_plan.a: No. An auto landing page drops the site menu and the inventory links, and the only way forward is the action the page asks for. Keep the dealership's name and phone number in view so the shopper knows who they are booking with. The idea is not specific to car sales: a nonprofit landing page cuts its menu so a donor sees one ask.

faq_plan.q: What should an auto repair landing page ask before booking?
faq_plan.a: The car's year and model, the service wanted, and a time. An auto repair landing page can leave the VIN and the description of the noise for drop-off, when the service writer can ask follow-up questions in person. Ask for a mobile number too if you plan to send a reminder the day before.

faq_plan.q: Should each listing get its own automotive landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the listing has its own ad. A car landing page for one vehicle carries its price and mileage above the photos and the test drive slots, and the ad for that car points straight at it. When the car sells, mark it sold and link to a similar one. A shopper who clicks an old ad then still finds something to book.

faq_plan.q: Do new and used inventory need separate automotive landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when they run as separate ads. A used car landing page sells one specific vehicle with its mileage and history, while a new page sells a model and its trims. Each page can then repeat exactly what its ad said, which is one habit every high converting landing page shares.

faq_plan.q: How quickly should leads from automotive landing pages get a reply?
faq_plan.a: Aim for the same business day at the latest, and within the hour during opening hours. Set that target before launch and name a backup for days off. The app Emergent builds can send each request to the consultant as a Slack or email alert, with a reminder and an escalation if it sits unanswered.

faq_plan.q: Should an automotive landing page show the price?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Show the same price as the ad: the number a shopper saw online should be the one they hear at the dealership. Leaving it off pushes price questions to the phone before anyone books. On a landing page for a used car, put the mileage right next to the price, since the buyer weighs the two together.

faq_plan.q: Where does an automotive landing page fit in a dealer's marketing?
faq_plan.a: It sits between the ad and the showroom visit. The ad brings a shopper to one car or offer, the page turns the click into a booking, and the follow-up gets the shopper in the door. Seen end to end, it works like a sales funnel landing page with the test drive as the last step. An app built with Emergent can show live counts of bookings by ad source.
